subject.title: [Feature]: 内置健壮性机制：Watchdog、全局错误处理、自动恢复

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in Gateway watchdog/recovery ladder, and which recovery actions should be default, opt-in, or out of scope?
rationale: The request crosses process supervision, config schema, doctor repair, notifications, degraded startup, and security-sensitive operator authority, so source inspection cannot safely choose permanent product semantics.

options.title: Design opt-in core recovery
options.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

options.title: Split into canonical subissues
options.body: Replace the broad umbrella with separate issues for process watchdog, health schema, error policy, degraded startup, and notifications.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Close the core request and document supervisor, plugin, or operator-owned recovery patterns instead.

recommendation.title: Design opt-in core recovery
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open while maintainers define a narrow opt-in recovery policy and split implementation into smaller owned follow-ups.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Gateway lifecycle, health, and recovery-adjacent history makes this the strongest routing candidate for the product boundary decision.
